assessments.rationale: Both analogies describe multiple drones sharing a map, broadcasting updates, and instant adjustment, mirroring cache coherence’s multiple caches, shared memory, and propagation of reads/writes. Their content coverage, structural consistency, and conceptual distance are essentially identical.

Each analogy uses chefs with a shared recipe book, instant sharing of a salt adjustment, and uniform seasoning, which aligns closely with the description’s multiple caches, shared state, and immediate update. No difference in coverage, mapping consistency, or abstraction level.

Analogy A mentions a library reservation system and directly maps ‘memory line’ to ‘catalog entry’, preserving the core ideas of shared copies and flag updates, giving higher content coverage and clearer structural mapping. Analogy B introduces many cross‑domain type changes (likes, feeds) making it more conceptually distant, thus higher M, and both analogies inject cache‑coherence terms into the source, flagged as target terminology injection.

Analogy A accurately reflects immediate propagation of availability updates across library branches, matching the description’s guarantee of a compatible view. Analogy B describes delayed or missing propagation, contradicting coherence, so A outperforms B on coverage, mapping consistency, and stays closer conceptually.

Analogy A uses processor cores, addresses, and cache updates, directly mirroring the description’s technical elements, giving higher content coverage and a tighter structural analogy. Analogy B’s traffic‑light metaphor is more abstract, increasing conceptual distance (higher M) while providing weaker mapping.

Analogy A correctly models write‑propagation and invalidation in a distributed database, aligning with cache‑coherence behavior. Analogy B reverses the operation, breaking the intended consistency, so A has superior coverage and mapping. Both reside in the same domain, so their conceptual distance is comparable.
